text:
alex: Heads-up — planning a rolling PSU phase resync + BMC microcycle in us-east1-rack-23. Window: Tue 03/02 00:30-02:30 UTC. Scope: aurora-gpu pool and burst-aurora shards in that rack. Plan is sequential PSU soft power-cycle per node, graceful drain, reboot, KV/prefix cache reseed, then uncordon. Will run a canary first. tagging oncall for visibility @oncall-bot

maria: Which exact node list? any dedicated customer shards in that rack?

alex: Node list attached in the runbook (shared to infra-runbooks). Short answer: 12 GPU nodes, 2 of them are reserved-standby for dedicated customers (we'll avoid draining their active workloads; we'll move tenants to reserve fleet and use our reserved backfill policy). No forced evictions.

jamaal: Throughput impact? we need SLO numbers to redistribute routing.

alex: Expect ~5-15% slot reduction transiently for each cohort during its 10-15m reboot. We'll rely on routing fallback to medium-quant models and reserved backfill. Canary will validate 3 requests/sec p50 latency baseline. If >20% latency regression, abort and roll back.

emily: Procedure ack. Can you paste the drain command you want ops to run so I can script it into the runbook?

alex: sure — using infractl for consistency:

```bash
# graceful drain with 30m timeout, skip evict for reserved tenants
infractl node drain --node $NODE --pool aurora-gpu --mode graceful --timeout 1800 --skip-evict-tags reserved
infractl node reboot --node $NODE --wait 600
infractl kv-seed --pool aurora-gpu --node $NODE --paths /kv/prefixes/top-5000 --parallel 4
```

ryan: Will we pre-warm prefix/KV cache across the cohort to avoid regen costs? last time we saw big token regen spikes.

alex: Yes — after reboot we run a targeted kv-seed against the canary and then progressively seed the cohort with parallelism=4. We also keep the persistent prefix cache on the reserve fleet so routing can hit warm caches.

product-ops: Heads-up — two customers (ACME / FinBlox) have hard SLAs in us-east1. We'll send customer comms and A/B mitigate routes during the window.

maria: Cost question: backfilling with reserve fleet will add compute spend. Rough estimate?

alex: Estimated additional spend ~ $450-700/hr during the window depending on parallelism. Finance signoff received up to $1,200 for this event. We'll tag resources with cost-center=psu-resync.

jamaal: I'll wire up short-lived alerts: pod_shed > 3% for >5m, model_fallback_rate > 10%, and 95th token latency spike. If any trigger, we pause next cohort and escalate.

oncall-bot: Reminder set — scheduled maintenance reminder will post 30m before window.

emily: I'll own runbook execution and post live status updates in #eng-infra during the window. Can someone own customer updates?

product-ops: I will. We'll push a targeted comm at T-24h and T-1h, include recommended action for customers (switch to regional fallback or enable degraded SLO tolerances).

ryan: One last ask — can we add a canary to the routing policy to prefer reserve backfill for low-priority workloads first? minimizes user-visible regressions.

alex: Good call. I'll update the routing policy to prefer reserved-backfill for priority=low and add a temporary weight shift of 20% for 1hr.

emily: :thumbsup: ok let's lock in the runbook and do a final run through with SRE tomorrow 16:00 UTC.

alex: Thanks all — will post final node list and playbook after the run-through. If you have immediate objections, flag now.
